text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Major-General Shaul Mofaz named Israeli deputy chief of staff.
- Ex-Navy chief suspected of bribery.
- Israeli-Palestinian talks to resume "within days".
- Interior Ministry, archaeologists demand delay on Ras al-Amoud Jewish settler enclave.
- Aide to Communications Minister Limor Livnat: Merrill Lynch deal for Bezeq could have been handled better.
- May jobless rate at three-year peak.
GLOBES
- Record unemployment in May at 7.7 percent.
- Bank of Israel leaves interest rates unchanged despite recommendation to raise them by 0.3 percent.
HAARETZ
- United States weighs imposing series of diplomatic steps. Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat tells his police in Hebron: Prepare for a long struggle against Israel.
- Israeli foreign ministry says number of Palestinians working in Israel is highest in two years.
MAARIV
- Talks renewed with Palestinians; joint committees begin to operate. Israel: "This is a renewal of negotiations". Palestinians: "These are but confidence-building measures".
- A near army training disaster: Shell explodes near group of reservists.
- Treasury weighs immediate steps for renewing growth: progress on projects, confronting unemployment and tax reform.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Negotiations resume between Israel and the Palestinians.
- Poll shows 75 percent of Bedouins prefer jail over military service.
- Bezeq Telecom workers threaten to resume strike.
- Knesset bill would allow for casinos in Israel.
